title: Molle Mystery Theatre
paragraphs: A mystery and suspense anthology presenting standalone crime and thriller dramas, often framed by the program's criminologist-commentator Geoffrey Barnes.

NBC mystery/suspense anthology built around standalone literary and original crime dramas. The recurring criminologist-commentator Geoffrey Barnes framed many broadcasts; Peter Lorre and other celebrity hosts also appear in surviving programs. The frozen GRH snapshot ends in June 1948 before the later post-Molle continuation.

GRH documents the program through Early NBC Mystery Theatre (September 7, 1943 to December 21, 1943) on [[org|org.f2f0561f0ce2ddc5|NBC Radio Network]] and Molle Mystery Theatre NBC era (December 28, 1943 to June 25, 1948) on [[org|org.f2f0561f0ce2ddc5|NBC Radio Network]].

Among the most extensively documented contributors in the GRH holdings are [[person|bernard-lenrow|Bernard Lenrow]] (host on 48 recordings and performer on 8 recordings), Dan Seymour (announcer on 37 recordings, commercial spokesman on 1 recording, and performer on 1 recording), Alexander Semmler (composer on 25 recordings and conductor on 25 recordings), Peter Lorre (host on 11 recordings), Cornell Woolrich (writer on 5 recordings, author on 4 recordings, and performer on 1 recording), Jack Miller (music on 5 recordings, composer on 4 recordings, and conductor on 3 recordings), and George Putnam (announcer on 4 recordings and commercial spokesman on 3 recordings).
The program is also connected in the archive to [[org|org.f2f0561f0ce2ddc5|NBC Radio Network]] (broadcast on network) and [[org|org.4798d1172deaae2c|Armed Forces Radio Service]] (rebroadcast by).

Its indexed subjects and listening characteristics include murder and homicide, psychological fear, obsession and madness, blackmail, greed and coercion, courtroom, jury and legal jeopardy, supernatural, occult and haunting, and poisoning and toxic murder methods.
GRH also places the series in documented historical contexts including AFRS Mystery Playhouse redistribution, Sponsor-branded network mystery, and Literary mystery adaptation culture.

Programs with especially strong personnel connections in the GRH knowledge graph include [[show|columbia-workshop|Columbia Workshop]] (37 shared credited people), [[show|words-at-war|Words at War]] (30 shared credited people), [[show|cbs-radio-mystery-theater|CBS Radio Mystery Theater]] (22 shared credited people), [[show|the-shadow|The Shadow]] (22 shared credited people), and [[show|inner-sanctum-mysteries|Inner Sanctum Mysteries]] (23 shared credited people).
